source.description:
PROBLEM
The MCP server uses StdioServerTransport (src/server.ts:244) and owns NativeActivationHost as an in-process field (src/server.ts:135). Stdio is connection-scoped: when the client disconnects the process exits, the host goes with it, and EVERY live native Specialist dies mid-flight.

That contradicts properties the PRD states explicitly. Section 1 requires a Specialist to be 'persistent' and 'resumable'. native-host.ts's own docstring says 'Session lifetime deliberately exceeds turn lifetime: reaching agent_settled makes a Specialist waiting and resumable, never disposed. Disposal is an explicit act.' Under stdio, disposal is NOT an explicit act — a dropped client disposes everything, silently, with no forensic settle and no lease release.

TO BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THE PRD DOES AND DOES NOT SAY: it never names a transport. 'streamable', 'http', 'sse' and 'stdio' each appear ZERO times. So this is not a violation of a named-transport requirement; it is a violation of the persistence and resumability requirements the PRD does state, which stdio plus an in-process host cannot satisfy. The stronger argument is the property one, and it does not depend on which protocol revision is current.

HOW THIS GOT MISSED: unitAI-rrdnt.33 (Phase 13) validated that the tools WORK over MCP — a real stdio client against the built dist server reaching state 'running' with a real pi_session_id. It never tested that an activation SURVIVES the client going away. Phase 13 was closed on tool reachability, not on lifetime. I closed it; this is my miss.

SUCCESS
A native activation survives the MCP client disconnecting and reconnecting, and remains resumable — or the coupling is documented as intended with its consequence stated wherever persistence is claimed.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

SCOPE
src/server.ts transport selection and host ownership. The decision about whether the host outlives the connection belongs in this bead.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the Pi extension, which is unaffected — its host lives in the pi process and has no MCP connection to lose. Does not change tool semantics.

CONSTRAINTS
The SDK in tree is @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0, whose LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25 and which also speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 and 2024-10-07. Our server pins nothing and takes the SDK default. Streamable HTTP with a session id is the transport that permits reconnection and parallel clients; moving to it is necessary but NOT sufficient — if the host stays a field on the server object, a process restart still kills every activation. The lifetime question is separate from the transport question and must be answered explicitly.
Do not treat 'the connection came back' as 'the activation survived'. That is the same inference-from-absence the uncertain-workspace design refuses everywhere else.

VALIDATION
1. Dispatch a native activation over MCP, drop the client, reconnect, and observe the activation still present and resumable.
2. A dropped client that DOES kill activations produces forensic settle events and releases workspace leases, rather than vanishing silently.

OUTPUT
Either a transport plus host-lifetime change that satisfies (1), or a documented decision with the consequence stated wherever the PRD's persistence claim is repeated.

REFERENCES
Raised by the operator 2026-09-08. Related: unitAI-rrdnt.33 (Phase 13, closed on tool reachability), unitAI-rrdnt.10 (which already demoted MCP as the Claude push transport after finding Claude Code's MCP client lacks the needed surfaces).
source.notes:
TRANSPORT AVAILABILITY CHECKED 2026-09-08, against the packages rather than from memory. The target is MCP spec 2026-07-28 (stateless connections), per the operator.

  installed:  @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0
              LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'
              SUPPORTED = ['2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26','2024-11-05','2024-10-07']
  latest published: 1.30.0 — fetched and unpacked to check
              LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'  (unchanged)
              '2026-07-28' appears ZERO times in its types.js

So the official TypeScript SDK does NOT yet speak 2026-07-28, even at head. Upgrading 1.29.0 -> 1.30.0 buys nothing for this bead. That reorders the work:

  1. The HOST LIFETIME fix is available NOW and is the larger half of the defect. Decoupling NativeActivationHost from the server object means a dropped client stops killing activations regardless of which transport is underneath. This bead's SUCCESS can be met on the current transport.
  2. The TRANSPORT move is blocked on the SDK, not on us. Options when it matters: wait for SDK support, implement 2026-07-28 outside the SDK, or move to Streamable HTTP on 2025-11-25 — which already permits reconnection and parallel clients and is a strict improvement on stdio even though it is not the target spec.

Do NOT do (2) before (1). A stateless transport in front of a host that still dies with its process just relocates the failure.

Re-check the SDK before starting: this reading is from 2026-09-08 and a version bump is exactly the kind of fact that goes stale.
DEFERRED by operator decision 2026-09-08 — the transport migration is a large piece of work in its own right and MCP is not the Pi coordinator's path.

CARRIED FORWARD, so the deferral is not read as 'no problem here': the HOST LIFETIME half is independent of the transport and is the larger half of the defect. NativeActivationHost is a field on the MCP server object, so process exit disposes every live Specialist with no forensic settle and no lease release. That is fixable on stdio today and does not wait for the SDK.

If MCP is picked up again for Claude and non-pi agents, do the lifetime decoupling FIRST. A stateless transport in front of a host that still dies with its process only relocates the failure.
source.title: MCP runs on stdio with an in-process host, so a dropped client kills every live Specialist
